title: Quantum Simulation of Detuning-Controlled Proximity-Induced Localization and Reentrant Delocalization in a Quasiperiodic Ladder
authors: Mrinal Kanti Giri, Shih Tai-Ming, Pinaki Sengupta, Pochung Chen
abstract: We demonstrate proximity-induced localization and re-entrant delocalization in a detuned quasiperiodic ladder. In the weak-quasiperiodic regime, where uncoupled Aubry-André chains are extended, a staggered detuning applied to only one leg induces localization in the neighboring leg through inter-leg hybridization. With further increasing detuning, the pure chain re-enters a delocalized regime, producing a delocalized-localized-delocalized sequence without directly modifying its quasiperiodic potential. We identify these regimes using static localization diagnostics and demonstrate experimentally accessible dynamical signatures on IBM Quantum hardware: strongly suppressed wavefunction spreading in the proximity-localized regime and its re-entrant recovery at larger detuning. These results establish leg-selective detuning as a programmable control knob for inducing and reversing localization in coupled quasiperiodic systems.
summary: This work explores how detuning can control localization and delocalization in a quasiperiodic ladder system. By applying detuning selectively to one leg, the researchers induce localization in the coupled neighbor, which can then re-enter a delocalized state. The findings are validated using both theoretical diagnostics and real-time quantum simulations on quantum hardware.
main_problem: The study investigates proximity-induced localization (PIL) and subsequent re-entrant delocalization in coupled quasiperiodic ladder systems.
main_result: The research demonstrates that applying a staggered detuning to one leg can induce localization in the neighboring leg, and further detuning can cause the system to re-enter a delocalized state, controllable via leg-selective detuning.
method: The study uses both static numerical diagnostics (IPR, NPR) and real-time quantum simulations on IBM Quantum hardware to measure wavefunction spreading.
model_or_system: The model is a two-leg Aubry-André (AA) ladder governed by a Hamiltonian involving intra-leg hopping, inter-leg coupling, and a staggered detuning ($\Delta$) applied to one leg.
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio ($	ext{IPR}$), Normalized Participation Ratio ($	ext{NPR}$), Mean-Square Displacement ($	ext{MSD}$), and Participation Entropy ($S_{	ext{PE}}^2$).
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), inter-leg coupling ($K$), and quasiperiodic potential strength ($\lambda$). Key regimes include weak and strong coupling limits.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to qubits for quantum simulation and uses post-selection techniques to focus on the single-particle sector.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams ($\lambda-\Delta$ plane) showing localization regimes, and show leg-resolved diagnostics ($\langle	ext{IPR}angle_{\ell}, \langle	ext{NPR}angle_{\ell}$) versus $\Delta$ to distinguish different physical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the coupled AA ladder Hamiltonian and analyzing localization diagnostics in different coupling limits, to demonstrating PIL and re-entrant delocalization using both static calculations and time-resolved quantum simulations.
why_interesting: The ability to programmatically control localization/delocalization using detuning in a quasiperiodic setting provides a powerful platform for studying transport and many-body physics in engineered quantum materials.
